Q: Java Thread: Real world Application Example A:

@Kayaman commented:

It can be done, but it would be a very poor example of multi-threading.

Here's why.

The unit of useful work that can be done in parallel is (in essence) converting the integers in the lists into strings. That is non-trivial ... but still relatively small.

Against that, you need to need to weigh the overheads of implementing parallelism. These include:

  • The overheads of creating and starting the Thread objects1 that will do the computations that are parallelized, along with the thread pool / executor service that will manage them.

  • The overheads of dispatching work to the threads.

  • The overheads of retrieving the results from the threads in the required order.

(Note that the thread and thread pool setup overheads can be amortized if you are going to print multiple lists. But your problem statement doesn't say there are multiple lists.)

Finally, the process of outputting the strings cannot be parallelized. Java output streams and buffered output streams are synchronized objects. Mutexes are used to stop overlapping write (etc) operations that might result in corrupted output.

If you take all of these into account, your example is not a good use-case for multi-threading.

Please refer to other answers for examples of how to use multi-threading to solve this problem ... bearing in mind that it doesn't really "help".

1 - Java 21+ virtual threads are not designed for this kind of problem.

Q: In C++ why the compiler is not giving any warning if same parameter is in surrounding scope and parameter list A:

Gcc warns about unused variables with -Wall -Werror:

<source>: In function 'void test()':
<source>:3:9: error: unused variable 'i' [-Werror=unused-variable]
    3 |     int i = 0;
      |         ^
<source>:9:9: error: unused variable 'j' [-Werror=unused-variable]
    9 |     int j = lambda(1);
      |         ^
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
Compiler returned: 1

That already hints at the issue.

You get the desired warning if you enable it via -Wshadow:

<source>: In lambda function:
<source>:4:27: error: declaration of 'i' shadows a previous local [-Werror=shadow]
    4 |     auto lambda = [&](int i)
      |                       ~~~~^
<source>:3:9: note: shadowed declaration is here
    3 |     int i = 0;
      |         ^
<source>: In function 'void test()':
<source>:3:9: error: unused variable 'i' [-Werror=unused-variable]
<source>:9:9: error: unused variable 'j' [-Werror=unused-variable]
    9 |     int j = lambda(1);
      |         ^
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
Compiler returned: 1

I expect other compilers to have flags to the same effect.

The lesson to learn is that warnings have to be enabled. And that -Wall does not actually enable all warnings.

Q: How do I change the IntelliJ IDEA default JDK? A:

Another thing is that you can have misconfigured JDK.

Go to Project Settings -> Project -> Click Edit on SDKs then you'll have list of your JDKs. Please make sure that the one that you use have non empty list of files in Classpath or Sourcepath sections, for whatever reason one of my JDKs pointed to proper path, but had all it's source files empty.

Q: Random generated string detection A:

You asked:

I thought there would be a ready-made solution for this, but I unfortunately cannot find one.

So I need recommendation for such free tools - if it is some model, I can host it and run it.

https://github.com/casics/nostril

Nostril is the Nonsense String Evaluator: a Python module that infers whether a given short string of characters is likely to be random gibberish or something meaningful.

https://huggingface.co/madhurjindal/autonlp-Gibberish-Detector-492513457

State-of-the-art gibberish detection model that accurately identifies nonsensical text, spam, and incoherent input in English. Built with DistilBERT and AutoNLP, this model achieves 97.36% accuracy in multi-class text classification, making it the ideal solution for content moderation, chatbot input validation, and text quality assurance.
